title: Annotator decision log and rotation protocol
content:
Purpose
This working doc defines a lightweight decision-log template plus a rotation/adjudication protocol for new annotators and adjudicators during applied-ML onboarding. The goal is to capture the rationale behind difficult labels, accelerate calibration, and provide auditable examples for regression investigations. This is intended primarily for: onboarding cohorts, calibration sprints, and intermittent IAA (inter-annotator agreement) audits.

Scope and audience
- Audience: labelers, adjudicators, onboarding leads, dataset owners, evaluation engineers.
- Scope: binary and multi-class content labels used for model onboarding evals (safety flags, factuality judgments, intent classification, reranking relevance). Not a replacement for full annotation schema docs — this is the operational log and dispute protocol.

High-level principles
1) Capture minimal structured context for each contentious case (why it was hard; which rubric rule applied). Keep entries short but explicit.
2) Prefer examples over abstract rules: every rule should be illustrated by 1–3 anchor examples in the log.
3) Keep adjudication decisions reversible with an audit trail — include who made the final call and the tie-break reason.
4) Use a rolling calibration cadence: weekly during onboarding then monthly thereafter for samples of live labels.

Decision log template (CSV-friendly single-line per case)
We expect each entry to fit in one row for easy ingestion. Use the following columns exactly (pipe-separated is fine for human readability):
- case_id | task_type | original_input_snippet | labeler_ids | labeler_labels | adjudicator_id | final_label | rule_anchor | short_reason | timestamp | followup_tag
Example row: 
ml-case-20240201-178 | factuality-check | "Claim: Jora was acquired in 2019" | jamal_o, mei_zhang | disagree, agree | alicia_park | disagree | factuality-anchor-2 | source-check failed, company timeline shows acquisition 2021 | 2024-02-01T14:03Z | needs-factfeed
Field guidance (short)
- case_id: unique short id (project prefix + date + sequence).
- task_type: e.g., factuality-check, toxicity, intent-class, rerank-relevance.
- original_input_snippet: 1–3 sentence excerpt sufficient to reproduce the judgment. Redact PHI.
- labeler_ids: comma-separated short handles.
- labeler_labels: labels in same order as labeler_ids. Use canonical labels (see label set below).
- adjudicator_id: who adjudicated (if any). Leave blank if unresolved.
- final_label: canonical final label. If unresolved, use UNRESOLVED.
- rule_anchor: link or short id to the specific rubric rule or anchor example that justified the decision (e.g., "toxicity-2b-anchor" or a Confluence anchor).
- short_reason: 1–2 phrases explaining the decision (e.g., "explicit slur; target protected class").
- timestamp: ISO date-time of adjudication or finalization.
- followup_tag: optional tags for dataset owners (e.g., needs-review, model-regress, policy-escalation).

Label sets and canonical naming (examples)
Provide canonical names so logs are consistent:
- factuality-check: {AGREE, DISAGREE, UNCERTAIN}
- toxicity: {SAFE, BORDERLINE, TOXIC}
- intent-class: {INFORMATIONAL, NAVIGATIONAL, TRANSACTIONAL, OTHER}
- rerank-relevance: {RELEVANT, MARGINALLY_RELEVANT, IRRELEVANT}
Use uppercase tokens in logs.

Short adjudication rubrics (operational, not exhaustive)
- Factuality-check: AGREE if the claim can be verified by reputable public sources or primary documents within two steps (Wikipedia-level ok). DISAGREE if clear contradicting sources exist or claim conflicts with canonical timelines. UNCERTAIN when evidence is thin or depends on ambiguous phrasing.
- Toxicity: TOXIC when the text contains explicit slurs, credible direct harassment, or dehumanizing content. BORDERLINE for implicit hostility, veiled slurs, or strong profanity without target. SAFE when profanity absent or clearly non-targeted (e.g., quoted neutral context).
- Intent-class: class by dominant user intent. If mixed, pick OTHER and add short_reason explaining ambiguity.
- Rerank-relevance: RELEVANT requires substantive overlap in task or answer; MARGINALLY_RELEVANT for partial match; IRRELEVANT for no useful overlap.

Adjudication flow and tie-breaking
1) Two-labeler primary workflow: every case is labeled by two independent annotators. If labels agree, entry is final.
2) Disagreement: escalate to a dedicated adjudicator. Adjudicator reviews both labels, the snippet, and relevant rubric anchors, then selects final_label and writes short_reason.
3) If adjudicator feels the rubric is insufficient, they may mark final_label as UNRESOLVED and request rubric update. This must generate a ticket (linked_artifacts preferred).
4) Tie-break policy for absent adjudicator: the senior onboarding lead (rotation lead) acts as tie-breaker. Annotators should not self-adjudicate conflicts.

Adjudicator rotation protocol (on-call style)
- Two-week rotations. Each rotation has 1 primary adjudicator and 1 backup.
- Handover doc at rotation start: list of active unresolved cases, outstanding followups, and two anchor examples updated in the shared calibration doc.
- Mandatory weekly 30-min sync for the rotation pair during onboarding weeks. After 6 weeks of cohort-independent labeling, cadence may drop to biweekly.

Calibration exercises (practical runbook)
- Week 0 (cohort start): run a 40-case calibration bundle. Each new annotator labels the bundle independently. Compute pairwise agreement matrix; any annotator with Cohen's kappa < 0.6 must re-do a second bundle and meet with a reviewer.
- Ongoing: sample 2% of annotations (min 100 cases/month) for spot-check calibration. Use the decision-log to pick high-disagreement categories preferentially.

IAA measurement and thresholds
- Primary metric: Cohen's kappa for binary/multi-class tasks. For ordinal tasks, use weighted kappa. For ranked relevance, use pairwise NDCG concordance sample.
- Thresholds (guideline): kappa >= 0.7 = production-good; 0.6–0.69 = acceptable with monitoring; < 0.6 = remediation required.
- When IAA falls, run an immediate 50-case focused calibration targeting low-agreement buckets (e.g., toxicity:BORDERLINE). Update anchor examples.

Examples and anchor library (short set — add to Confluence)
- factuality-anchor-1: "Claim: Redwood launched Dedicated in 2022" -> AGREE (press release + changelog present).
- factuality-anchor-2: "Claim: Company X acquired Jora in 2019" -> DISAGREE (public sources show acquisition 2021).
- toxicity-2b-anchor: explicit slur against protected class -> TOXIC.
- toxic-vs-borderline-anchor: profanity with no target -> BORDERLINE unless directed at an individual.
Each anchor in the Confluence library must include: (1) short text, (2) canonical label, (3) adjudication note, (4) links to policy sources.

Operational notes for regression investigations
- When a model regression is flagged, ingestion engineers will pull the decision-log for the affected prompt sets. Decision-log entries are the primary artifact for matching human labels to pre-regression anchor examples.
- If adjudication records are missing for high-impact cases, treat as data-quality incident and escalate to data ops.

Record-retention and privacy
- Decision logs are internal and retained for 2 years by default. Redact any personal data per GDPR policy before sharing externally. Use followup_tag: privacy-redact for cases that require masking.

Templates and quick commands
- Quick command for unresolved: tag row with followup_tag=needs-rubric, create JIRA JIRA-ML-xxxx with case_id in title.
- Quick export: run export script in repo "labeling-scripts" to produce a CSV digest for monthly IAA runs (PR link in linked_artifacts).

Onboarding checklist (actionable)
- Day 1: read canonical labeling guide and this decision-log template.
- Day 2: shadow labelling session and run first 40-case calibration bundle.
- Day 4: review initial disagreements with rotation lead; add 3 new anchors based on cohort confusions.
- End of week 2: must pass kappa >= 0.6 or repeat bundle + remediation session.

Open questions for review (items to discuss in the next applied-ml annotation working meeting)
- Should we require an adjudicator rationale to reference at least one anchor id for every non-trivial decision? (Pros: traceability. Cons: friction.)
- Is two-week rotation cadence sustainable as labeling scales to multiple projects?
- Define an automated flag for 'high-impact' cases that demands a second adjudicator review (e.g., public-facing prompts).

Appendix — quick CSV example (human-readable)
case_id|task_type|original_input_snippet|labeler_ids|labeler_labels|adjudicator_id|final_label|rule_anchor|short_reason|timestamp|followup_tag
ml-20240308-11|toxicity|"You're a pathetic loser"|mei_l, evan_c|TOXIC, TOXIC|alicia_park|TOXIC|toxicity-2b-anchor|direct insult at individual|2024-03-08T11:22Z|
ml-20240201-178|factuality-check|"Claim: Jora was acquired in 2019"|jamal_o, mei_zhang|DISAGREE, AGREE|alicia_park|DISAGREE|factuality-anchor-2|contradicted by press release|2024-02-01T14:03Z|needs-factfeed

If anything in this doc contradicts the canonical schema (label set documents under Confluence), the canonical schema wins — this doc is operational. Please add new anchor examples into the Confluence anchor library and link them from the rule_anchor field.

Contact and ownership

- Onboarding rotation coordinator: Jamal Ortiz

End of doc
